STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CARE FOR THE ENVIRONMENT
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Caring for plants- Observing flower beds
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
  observe flower beds
  point out which flower beds are watered
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
  How do we know when flower beds have been watered?
  How do flowers look like when they have not been watered?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Critical thinking and  Responsibility Environmental education
 problem solving
  Communication and
 collaboration
LEARNING RESOURCES
Photographs displaying flower beds
Sample flower beds at school
Pencils, crayons, books for drawing
Enrich Yourself Environmental activities Teachers guide pg.81-82
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs/groups
INTRODUCTION
Do a brainstorming activity with learners.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
Step 1: Learners to take a walk around the school as they observe flower beds available
Step 2: Guide learners to determine which flowerbeds were not watered.
Step 3: Guide learners to look at the picture of a flowerbed in their books Guide them to appreciate the flowers that
have been watered
Step 4: Guide learners to look at a picture and appreciate that the flowerbed looks fresh and beautiful because it has
been watered.
SUMMARY
Make summary points/notes
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Guide learners to recite the poem.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to observe flowerbeds during the day at different times.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CARE FOR THE ENVIRONMENT
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Caring for animals- Animal feeds
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to identify common feeds for various domestic animals.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
  What do domestic animals eat?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Responsibility Environmental education
 collaboration Citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
A video clip showing animals feeding
Photographs showing different types of animals kept at home
Enrich Yourself Environmental activities Teachers guide pg.86-87
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs/groups
INTRODUCTION
Do a brainstorming activity with learners
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
Step 1: prepare a trip to the farm and let learners visit animal farms where there are animals and animal feeds.
Step 2: Guide learners to share and discuss different experiences about animal feeds.
Step 3: Guide learners to discuss what each animal in the pictures is eating on page 40 of their book.
Step 4: Learners to read the sentence under each picture after you and let them discuss other animal feed they know.
SUMMARY
Make summary points/notes
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and ask questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to talk to their parents/guardians on animal feeds.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CARE FOR THE ENVIRONMENT
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Managing waste responsibly- types of waste in a classroom
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to
  Identify types of waste in the classroom
  Safely sort out waste in the classroom for appropriate disposal
  Dispose of waste responsibly to limit risk to self, others and environment.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
  What types of waste are found in the classroom?
  How can we dispose of classroom waste responsibly?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Responsibility Environmental education
 collaboration Citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Samples of type of waste
Chart illustrating different types of waste
Pencils, crayons and drawing books
Pictures of common things used in handling waste e.g. broom, dust pan, gloves
Slogan on recycling
Enrich Yourself Environmental activities Teachers guide pg.92-94
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs/groups
INTRODUCTION
Do a brainstorming activity with learners
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
Step 1: Ask learners to move around the class and identify any litter on the floor, window panes.
Step 2: Write on the board every item noticed
Step 3: Learners to wear appropriate protective gear and collect waste found in the classroom
Step 4: Guide learners to identify the various types of waste in the class and guide them through activity on page 43
SUMMARY
Make summary points/notes
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to discuss among themselves about types of waste they have collected
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to draw and colour different types of waste in their classroom.

Learners to watch a video illustrating the different waste materials that are found in the home environment.

Charts showing different sources of light

Learners to work in pairs/groups

Do a brainstorming activity with learners

Make summary notes/points
